chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Abu Khalid al-Qammam, from Humran, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I ask you, may Allah improve you.' He said, 'Yes.'

So I said, 'I was in a certain state, and today I am in another state. I used to enter the land (go out to people) and invite the man, the two, and the woman, and Allah would rescue whom He willed; and today I do not invite anyone.'
He said, 'And there is no harm upon you if you leave between the people and their Lord. So whoever Allah intends to bring out from darkness to light, He brings him out.'
Then he said, 'And there is no harm upon you if you perceive goodness in someone, to introduce something to him with an introduction.'
I said, 'Inform me about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all the people.'
He said, 'From burning or drowning.' Then he was silent, then said, 'Its greatest interpretation is that you invite her, so she responds to you.'

key_terms.أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah improve you (a common address to the Imam)
key_terms.وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا: And whoever keeps it alive (referring to the soul/life)

ai.seo_question: What is the deeper interpretation of 'whoever keeps it alive' in Surah Al-Ma'idah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *al-amr bi-l-ma'ruf* (enjoining good), clarifying that active invitation is a means but ultimate guidance (*hidayah*) rests with Allah. The Imam’s dual explanation of the verse 'And whoever keeps it alive...' bridges the literal preservation of physical life with the spiritual revival of the believer (*mu'min*) through da'wah, a key exegetical nuance in Shia scholarship. This context validates the transition from active proselytizing to patient waiting, emphasizing that the spiritual 'life' of a soul is the ultimate objective of the caller.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Al Halby, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘Can I ask you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> (something)? May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Keep you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> well!’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

So I said, ‘I was upon a (particular) state, and today I am upon another state. I used to enter the land, so I would invite (to Religion) the man, and the two, and the woman, and Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Rescue the one whom He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> so Desired to; and today I am not inviting anyone’.

So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And there is nothing upon you if you were to leave between the people and their Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>. So the one whom Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Intends to Extract from darkness to Light, would Extract him’.
Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Nor is it upon you if you know of goodness from anyone that you introduce the thing to him with an introduction’.
I said, ‘Inform me about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:32] and whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all the people’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘From drowning or burning’. Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> was silent, then said: ‘Its magnificent interpretation is that you invite him, so he responds to it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al- Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al- Halabi from abu Khalid al-Qammat from Humran who has said the following:
“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Can I ask you a question, may Allah keep you well?’ He said, ‘Yes you may do so.’

I said, ‘I was in a particular condition and today I am in another condition. I would go in the land to invite one or two men and women (to our belief) and Allah would save whomever He wanted. Today I do not invite anyone.’
The Imam said, ‘It is no offense to you to leave people to their Lord. Whomever Allah wants to guide and take out of darkness to light He does so.’
The Imam then said, ‘It is not an offense to you if you sense good in someone to introduce an issue.’
1 then said, ‘Tell me about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘. . . to save a life is as great a virtue as to save all of mankind. . . .’ [5:32]
The Imam said, ‘It refers to burning or drowning someone. He then remained quiet and then said, ‘Its greatest case in point, is that one is invited (to the truth), and he accepts it.’”
